first_impression.reaction: Not what I expected from a wedding planner's site. No 'forever symbol of your love' opener, just four tests and a lot of GIA. I went to the FAQ first, it gave straight answers, so I went back and read most of the nine settings. I'm buying the ring, so this is actually useful.

journey.quote: Most ring guides rank settings by looks. This one asks what happens on a ski lift, a reef dive and a long-haul flight.
journey.reaction: Fair hook, and it's a criterion I can use. Fine.

journey.quote: **Skip it if:** maximum sparkle is the point. A bezel covers more of the edge than claws and lets in slightly less light.
journey.reaction: Every setting gets a 'skip it if'. That's the trade-off honesty I look for. Nobody's pretending one option is perfect.

journey.quote: Many rings sold as "tension style" quietly hold the stone with small hidden claws or a partial bezel, while a true tension setting relies on the metal's pressure alone.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of 'here's the catch' info I actually want. Gives me a question to ask the jeweller that they won't volunteer.

journey.section: Before a destination wedding: claw check and insurance
journey.quote: Book a setting check four to six weeks before you fly, so any re-tipping or tightening is done with time to spare.
journey.reaction: Everything else says 'GIA says'. This one doesn't. Where does four to six weeks come from? Sounds sensible, but it reads like house opinion dressed up next to sourced facts. Say so if it is.

journey.section: From the ring to the adventure: planning a wedding abroad
journey.quote: A ring chosen for the trail often comes with a wedding in the same spirit: a mountain lodge, a coastline, a long weekend that runs into the honeymoon.
journey.reaction: And here's the pivot to the sales bit. 'Often' based on what? It's a soft emotional bridge after nine sections of evidence. I can see the seam.

journey.section: From the ring to the adventure: planning a wedding abroad
journey.quote: If you would rather hand over the logistics, Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world' is a big claim with nothing behind it. And 'payments' is exactly where my alarm goes off. Do you handle supplier payments? Do you take a cut on them? What's your fee? Not a word.

unanswered_questions: How is Wedded Concierge paid: flat fee, percentage, or commission from venues and suppliers?
If Wedded Concierge handles 'payments', are supplier prices passed through at cost or marked up?
What does 'anywhere in the world' mean in practice? Any evidence, like a real wedding with the actual budget?
Where does the 'four to six weeks before you fly' timing come from, or is it your own recommendation?

turn_offs_found.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported scope claim, and mentions handling payments without saying how the fee or any supplier commissions work.

turn_offs_found.quote: When the ring is sorted and the conversation turns to where, your Wedded Advisor is a good person to have it with.
turn_offs_found.why: Second sales nudge tacked on after the FAQ. 'A good person to have it with' is warm fluff, not a reason.

would_share_with: My partner, as a shortlist tool for the ring itself
Maybe a mate who rock climbs and is ring shopping

cta_reaction.quote: [Talk to a Wedded Concierge about a wedding abroad](/wonderland-concierge).
cta_reaction.why: Credit where due: the CTA comes after the evidence, not before. But I came for ring settings and I'm not booking a sales call off a ring guide when the page tells me nothing about the fee model. I might remember the brand as one that cites its sources. That's it for now.

top_3_changes: Next to the Wedded Concierge mention, say plainly how you're paid (or link a 'how our fees work' page), especially since you say you handle payments.
Drop 'anywhere in the world' or back it with something concrete, like a real wedding with a dated budget.
Mark the 'four to six weeks before you fly' timing as your own recommendation, or source it like everything else.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, proof and fee model focus, plain voice
No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions and proof listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and fact markers treated as invisible
